camera_relocalization-0obstacle20106 (109)109 model ids listed; 0 exact duplicates counted once -> 109 models (bracket); 6 models are texture/colour variants of another listed model -> 106 distinct geometriesBDDL objects: floor.n.01_1, agent.n.01_1 only; goal = head-camera pose (no manipulated object). OBSTACLE = optional extra object for some instances: dropped on a free floor cell roughly midway along the init -> goal path so that the robot has to steer around it; never touched. Not in problem0.bddl and not placed by the sampler yet (sampler support pending; a spec block is ready in runlogs/obstacle_selection_20260912/spec_fragments.json: roles.obstacle.models = the picks, _pool = every valid model, _natural_scenes = where each category may be drawn). Test spec pins none yet (no obstacle role in the spec). Requirements: natural on the floor of at least one of the 7 candidate scenes (house_single_floor, house_double_floor_upper / _lower, Rs_int, restaurant_diner, hotel_suite_large, office_cubicles_right) and unremarkable in the middle of a room or corridor (bins, potted plants, cardboard boxes, laundry hampers, buckets, luggage, toys, stools, vacuum cleaners, carts), small enough to be dropped on a free floor cell without blocking a ~1 m corridor (R1Pro chassis half-diagonal 0.33 m) yet tall enough to be a real obstacle for the base and visible to the head camera, and stable in its canonical pose (placed as is, +z up). Selection = runlogs/obstacle_selection_20260912 (no grasp test): 96 candidate categories hand-picked from a geometry scan of every BEHAVIOR category with ready models (median footprint 0.12-0.9 m, height 0.10-1.7 m; candidate_scan.json) and the object inventory of the 7 scenes (scene_presence.json); 296 ready models (<= 12-16 per category) rendered in their canonical frame (renders/grids) and scored by 8 reviewers with review_contract.md: V visual 0-5, N naturalness as a mid-path floor obstacle 0-3 (3 = commonly stands in walkable space and is unremarkable mid-path, 2 = plausible but normally against a wall / small clutter, 1 = odd, 0 = not floor-standing / not in these scenes), S size fit 0-2 (2 = footprint 0.20-0.55 m and height 0.20-1.10 m, 1 = borderline, 0 = > 0.80 m footprint or < 0.12 m / < 0.10 m tall / > 1.70 m), rest_ok (stands stably, +z up; balls and lying / hanging models fail); score = 2V + 2N + S (max 18); valid = V >= 3, N >= 2, S >= 1, rest_ok. Round 1 = the 10 best categories (mean score of the two best valid models; >= 2 valid), round 2 = the next 5 (>= 2 valid), round 3 = the next 5 (>= 1 valid); rounds are ranking tiers - the obstacle is never manipulated, so no overlap rule with other tasks' categories (overlaps noted per category). EVERY valid model of the 20 selected categories is listed (109 rows: pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); invalid models are not listed. pair = the scenes the category is natural in (* = already present in that scene's files). Duplicate check: geometry signatures (duplicates.json). Reviewed but not selected (ranked in selection.md): highchair (good, 2 valid of 2 reviewed); box_of_fruit (weak, 2 valid of 2 reviewed); rocking_chair (weak, 4 valid of 4 reviewed); rubber_boot (weak, 4 valid of 4 reviewed); EVERY model with >= 1 AG-valid grasp is listed (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); models with no AG-valid grasp are not listed. Categories are ordered by their number of distinct geometries, descending. Duplicate check (select/duplicates.md): models judged the EXACT same asset count as one model in the counts and say 'exact duplicate of ...' in the duplicates column; texture/colour variants of one geometry are kept but marked 'same geometry as ...'.

disembedding-0target39161 (233)243 model ids listed; 10 exact duplicates counted once -> 233 models (bracket); 98 models are texture/colour variants of another listed model -> 161 distinct geometriesBDDL objects: 1 target (ontop tray_source at init -> ontop tray_dest at goal, released), distractor group (1..max_distractors models, same category or other categories), 2 trays, table, floor, agent. Grasps: antipodal tabletop pipeline (picked from its resting pose on the tray; must settle stably; the best single grasp matters most). Test spec pins box_of_cereal/iucshm (grasps.key box_of_cereal__iucshm). Selection = grasp-library test instances (runlogs/grasp_library_20260905/select/test_instances.md): 2 picks per category, score = 2G+2V+T+R (max 25; G grasp, V visual, T task fit, R robustness); round 1 = original curated plan, 2 = category reused from another task, 3 = new category (single-model categories allowed). EVERY model with >= 1 AG-valid grasp is listed (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); models with no AG-valid grasp are not listed. Categories are ordered by their number of distinct geometries, descending. Duplicate check (select/duplicates.md): models judged the EXACT same asset count as one model in the counts and say 'exact duplicate of ...' in the duplicates column; texture/colour variants of one geometry are kept but marked 'same geometry as ...'. Distractor pools: see the same_category_pool / distractor_pool rows below and the pair column of every target row (same-category pool size after removing the target and its look-alikes; other-category pool size and families). LOOK-ALIKE in the duplicates column = models that cannot be told apart from the robot's initial view; they are never drawn as distractors of each other.

disembedding-0same_category_pool39208 (259)33 look-alike groups (init view) across the same-category poolsSame-category distractor pool per target category (blocks below: category = target category; model count = look-alike groups (models)). At sampling time the target itself and every model in its LOOK-ALIKE group are removed (spec lookalike_groups). Method (runlogs/disembedding_distractors_20260911): candidates = every ready model of the category (same pool) and ready models of hand-curated related categories (other pool, closest first: e.g. forks / knives for spoons, rice / sugar boxes for cereal boxes), size-filtered for the source tray; each candidate was rendered alone on the source tray from the robot's head camera at the disembedding init stance (house_single_floor dining table, test trays; renders/) and settled for 60 physics steps; reviewer agents grouped same-category models that cannot be told apart in that view (review_contract.md, groups/; merged with the exact-duplicate groups of select/duplicates.md); every candidate was then validated with the instance sampler (validate_distractors.py: DisembeddingSampler.setup with the category's test pick as target + TaskSampler.run(1) with the candidate as the only distractor - sample, settle, BEHAVIOR checks, :init true, goal false, occlusion measurement, goal feasibility; results/). Pool = 20 candidates per target category: same-category look-alike groups first (a group counts as ONE candidate, at most 10 groups; all validated members of a selected group are listed so the group exclusion works whichever member is the target), related-category models fill the rest (at most 3 per category). selection = pool (in the 20) / reserve (validated, beyond the 20). Spec form: runlogs/disembedding_distractors_20260911/distractors_section.json (disembedding-0.distractors: pools.<category>.same_category / other_models, lookalike_groups). Target template failed on the test table (pools render-checked only): bar_soap.

disembedding-0distractor_pool39572 (572)Other-category distractor pool per target category (blocks below: category = TARGET category, model = <distractor category>/<model>, pair = why the category is related, tier 1 = closest). Drawn when generation.same_category_prob does not select the same-category pool. Method (runlogs/disembedding_distractors_20260911): candidates = every ready model of the category (same pool) and ready models of hand-curated related categories (other pool, closest first: e.g. forks / knives for spoons, rice / sugar boxes for cereal boxes), size-filtered for the source tray; each candidate was rendered alone on the source tray from the robot's head camera at the disembedding init stance (house_single_floor dining table, test trays; renders/) and settled for 60 physics steps; reviewer agents grouped same-category models that cannot be told apart in that view (review_contract.md, groups/; merged with the exact-duplicate groups of select/duplicates.md); every candidate was then validated with the instance sampler (validate_distractors.py: DisembeddingSampler.setup with the category's test pick as target + TaskSampler.run(1) with the candidate as the only distractor - sample, settle, BEHAVIOR checks, :init true, goal false, occlusion measurement, goal feasibility; results/). Pool = 20 candidates per target category: same-category look-alike groups first (a group counts as ONE candidate, at most 10 groups; all validated members of a selected group are listed so the group exclusion works whichever member is the target), related-category models fill the rest (at most 3 per category). selection = pool (in the 20) / reserve (validated, beyond the 20). Spec form: runlogs/disembedding_distractors_20260911/distractors_section.json (disembedding-0.distractors: pools.<category>.same_category / other_models, lookalike_groups).

Grasps: attachment_free pipeline (all gripper spheres >= 1 cm from the attachment meta-link, mating side fully uncovered). Pair = female partner(s) with the matching attachment meta-link type (BEHAVIOR meta-links, from runlogs/grasp_exp_20260904/category_table.json), listed for EVERY row (picks, alternates and candidates; filled 2026-09-11, before that only for the picks). '(no attachment meta-link)' = the model carries no attachment meta-link, so it has no partner and can never attach; it stays listed and counted as a graspable training candidate. '(not ready)' = partner has an unprocessed BEHAVIOR QA complaint (complaint type in the row note). Not-ready rule (2026-09-11): a model that is not ready itself, or whose partners are ALL not ready, stays listed but is NOT counted in the category / model counts and carries a 'NOT COUNTED' marker in its note; not-ready partners are likewise listed but not counted under the female role. All 30 male models are ready themselves; not counted for lack of a ready partner: cap/hbafeb [pick 1], cap/vnpjfn, cap/clhquh, blackberry/tvpfvb [pick 1] (blackberry keeps no counted model). cap/xxqyrt keeps 3 of its 4 partners (water_bottle/lzdzkk not ready). Picks are unchanged (they mirror select/test_instances.md), so cap/hbafeb and blackberry/tvpfvb currently have no usable partner and would need re-selection. Test spec pins cap/xxqyrt -> lemonade_bottle/yprkek (grasps.key cap__xxqyrt). Round-2 reversed pairs (female part grasped, cap fixed) were both dropped and are not listed: bottle_of_water/emquat (task_violation), soda_cup/vicaqs (no AG-valid grasp). Categories tested with NO AG-valid model, not listed: dartboard (round 1), license_plate (round 1), soda_cup (round 2), antlers (round 3), bow (round 3), fire_alarm (round 3), menu (round 3). Selection = grasp-library test instances (runlogs/grasp_library_20260905/select/test_instances.md): 2 picks per category, score = 2G+2V+T+R (max 25; G grasp, V visual, T task fit, R robustness); round 1 = original curated plan, 2 = category reused from another task, 3 = new category (single-model categories allowed). EVERY model with >= 1 AG-valid grasp is listed (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); models with no AG-valid grasp are not listed. Categories are ordered by their number of distinct geometries, descending. Duplicate check (select/duplicates.md): models judged the EXACT same asset count as one model in the counts and say 'exact duplicate of ...' in the duplicates column; texture/colour variants of one geometry are kept but marked 'same geometry as ...'.

configuration_matching-3 (attachment)floor00fixed scene object: house_single_floor: floor of dining_room_0; other scenes: floor of the room of the bound table (see the table row)
world_alignment-0 (table_surface)target20109 (125)125 model ids listed; 0 exact duplicates counted once -> 125 models (bracket); 26 models are texture/colour variants of another listed model -> 109 distinct geometriesBDDL objects: 1 target ontop the table (goal = orientation only, released), table, floor, agent. The object rests on the table with a vertical hinge through its CoM (TRO revolute constraint) and is pushed from a deviation of 20-70 deg back to the aligned yaw (long axis parallel to the table's front edge, front toward the robot); it must therefore have ONE readable yaw (asymmetric print / keys / handle), rest flat and stable, and fit on a table (0.12-0.50 m long, <= 0.10 m high). Test spec pins keyboard/hgtbot and keyboard/injrgc (front_axis +x, long_axis y). The frames below differ per category (and sometimes per model): sampler >= 1.4.1 takes generation.front_axis / long_axis as dicts keyed by '<category>/<model>' (ready-made in spec_fragments.json). Selection = runlogs/world_alignment_selection_20260911 (no grasp test: the object is pushed). Every ready model of the candidate categories was rendered in its canonical frame (renders/grids, up to 16 per category) and scored by 8 reviewers with review_contract.md: V visual 0-5, O orientation readability 0-3, F table fit 0-2; score = 2V + 2O + F (max 18); valid = V >= 3, O >= 2, F >= 1. Round 1 = 10 categories used by no other task (>= 2 valid models), round 2 = 5 more (may overlap other tasks' round-1 categories, >= 2 valid), round 3 = 5 more (any overlap, 1 valid model enough). EVERY valid model is listed (pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score; picks = the two best, pair rule prefers a visually different second model); invalid models are not listed. pair = canonical frame read from the renders (long axis x|y, front = side facing the robot when aligned). Blocks ordered by round, then category score (mean of the two best valid models). Duplicate check: geometry signatures of the listed models (duplicates.json; exact = identical geometry and identical diffuse textures). Reviewed but not selected: chess_set (weak, 1 valid of 2 reviewed); credit_card_terminal (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); first_aid_kit (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); griddle_pan (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); world_alignment-1 (world_vertical)target1864 (69)69 model ids listed; 0 exact duplicates counted once -> 69 models (bracket); 10 models are texture/colour variants of another listed model -> 64 distinct geometriesBDDL objects: 1 target hinged on a wall through its CoM (TRO revolute constraint, axis = wall normal; goal = straight orientation, released), wall, floor, agent. Hung with its centre at 1.45 m, started 15-45 deg off in the wall plane and pushed back by a lower corner from an arc 0.6-0.95 m in front; it must therefore have ONE readable upright orientation, be flat-backed and thin, 0.25-0.9 m across and natural on a wall. Test spec pins painting/dacihj and painting/ljabhq (front_axis +x, up +z, thin x = the sampler's assumed frame). Categories whose canonical frame lies flat (thin z: picture, license_plate, guitar, hanger, dartboard, ...) are hung with sampler >= 1.4.1's generation.up_axis / front_axis dicts keyed by '<category>/<model>' (ready-made in spec_fragments.json); the frames are in pair. Selection = runlogs/world_alignment_selection_20260911 (no grasp test: the object is pushed). Every ready model of the candidate categories was rendered in its canonical frame (renders/grids, up to 16 per category) and scored by 8 reviewers with review_contract.md: V visual 0-5, U up readability 0-3, H hangability 0-2; score = 2V + 2U + H (max 18); valid = V >= 3, U >= 2, H >= 1. Round 1 = 10 categories used by no other task (>= 2 valid models), round 2 = 5 more (may overlap other tasks' round-1 categories, >= 2 valid), round 3 = 5 more (any overlap, 1 valid model enough). EVERY valid model is listed (pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score; picks = the two best, pair rule prefers a visually different second model); invalid models are not listed. pair = canonical frame read from the renders (front = axis out of the wall, up = axis that points up when hung, thin = thinnest bbox axis). Blocks ordered by round, then category score (mean of the two best valid models). Duplicate check: geometry signatures of the listed models (duplicates.json; exact = identical geometry and identical diffuse textures). Reviewed but not selected: menu (weak, 3 valid of 6 reviewed); broom (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); bulletin_board (weak, 1 valid of 2 reviewed); tennis_racket (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); violin (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); hook_rack (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); wall_mounted_soap_dispenser (weak, 1 valid of 3 reviewed); antlers (drop, 0 valid of 2 reviewed); board (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); calendar (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); canvas (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); frame (drop, 0 valid of 2 reviewed); grocery_sign (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); hat (drop, 0 valid of 4 reviewed); holly_decoration (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); map (drop, 0 valid of 3 reviewed); mirror (drop, 0 valid of 6 reviewed); monitor (drop, 0 valid of 10 reviewed); pegboard (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); skateboard_deck (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); thermostat (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); wall_mounted_tv (drop, 0 valid of 15 reviewed); windshield (drop, 0 valid of 2 reviewed); wreath (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed).

world_alignment-1 (world_vertical)floor00fixed scene object: house_single_floor: floor of living_room_0; other scenes: floor of the room of the validated wall region (see the wall row)
world_alignment-2 (world_horizontal)target1863 (69)69 model ids listed; 0 exact duplicates counted once -> 69 models (bracket); 12 models are texture/colour variants of another listed model -> 63 distinct geometriesBDDL objects: 1 target hinged flat on a wall through its CoM (TRO revolute constraint, axis = wall normal; goal = LEVEL orientation, released), wall, floor, agent. Sibling of world_alignment-1 with the same hinge, 1.45 m hanging height, 15-45 deg init tilt in the wall plane and pushing from an arc 0.6-0.95 m in front; the object must therefore have ONE readable horizontal direction (a dominant long axis or reference edge: bars, rails, shelves, wide boards / signs, rods on display hooks), be flat against the wall and 0.25-0.9 m along that axis. A 180-deg ambiguity is fine (a plain bar is level either way; such models carry 'symmetric 180' in pair and the sampler adds the half turn about the front axis to the goal's orientation equivalences), a 90-deg one (square) is not. Test spec pins towel_rack/crivoa, towel_rack/kqrmrh. Frames per model in pair (sampler dict form ready-made in spec_fragments.json: generation.front_axis / up_axis / level_axis / symmetric_180). Selection = runlogs/world_horizontal_selection_20260912 (no grasp test). 135 ready models of 40 elongated wall / rod categories (candidate_categories.json: geometry scan of every BEHAVIOR category + wall / rod vocabulary) rendered in their canonical frame (renders/grids) and scored by 8 reviewers with review_contract.md: V visual 0-5, L level readability 0-3, H hangability 0-2; score = 2V + 2L + H (max 18); valid = V >= 3, L >= 2, H >= 1. Round 1 = up to 10 categories used by no other task (>= 2 valid models), round 2 = up to 5 more (may overlap other tasks' round-1 categories, incl. world_alignment-1's; >= 2 valid), round 3 = up to 5 more (any overlap, 1 valid model enough). EVERY valid model is listed (pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); invalid models are not listed. Each row notes the flat wall patch the model needs (its extents swept between a 45 deg tilt and level + 0.10 m); compare with the wall rows' patch sizes. Duplicate check: geometry signatures (duplicates.json). Reviewed but not selected: shovel (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); tennis_racket (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); bookcase_shelf (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); bulletin_board (weak, 1 valid of 2 reviewed); handle (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); hook_rack (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); longboard (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); rake (weak, 1 valid of 2 reviewed); trumpet (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); painting (weak, 2 valid of 6 reviewed); poster (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); wall_mounted_light (weak, 3 valid of 6 reviewed); board (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); golf_club (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); poker (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); skateboard_deck (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); violin (weak, 1 valid of 1 reviewed); air_conditioner (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); fishing_rod (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed); frame (drop, 0 valid of 2 reviewed); range_hood (drop, 0 valid of 6 reviewed); wall_mounted_loudspeaker (drop, 0 valid of 1 reviewed).

inter_object_relation_satisfaction-0 (ontop)target1054 (57)60 model ids listed; 3 exact duplicates counted once -> 57 models (bracket); 5 models are texture/colour variants of another listed model -> 54 distinct geometriesBDDL objects: target (grasped, placed ontop the partner, released), partner (unchanged), table, floor, agent; both poses measured only. Grasps: antipodal tabletop pipeline, object bottom left free for placing. Pair = partner category (small on small; 'scene' partners are fixed scene surfaces). Test spec pins pack_of_kielbasa/dgodnn -> platter/csanbr (grasps.key pack_of_kielbasa__dgodnn__t). Selection = grasp-library test instances (runlogs/grasp_library_20260905/select/test_instances.md): 2 picks per category, score = 2G+2V+T+R (max 25; G grasp, V visual, T task fit, R robustness); round 1 = original curated plan, 2 = category reused from another task, 3 = new category (single-model categories allowed). EVERY model with >= 1 AG-valid grasp is listed (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); models with no AG-valid grasp are not listed. Categories are ordered by their number of distinct geometries, descending. Duplicate check (select/duplicates.md): models judged the EXACT same asset count as one model in the counts and say 'exact duplicate of ...' in the duplicates column; texture/colour variants of one geometry are kept but marked 'same geometry as ...'.

Scene partners (countertop / desk / bed / couch) are fixed scene objects; object partners are listed per model below (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate as for the targets; PINNED = pinned in task_custom_lists.json). Partner MODELS (2026-09-11): the rows below list, per partner category, the ready models (no unprocessed knowledge-base complaint) that (a) the instance sampler can place on the scene supports validated for IORS by the table-selection run so far plus the test table (15 supports: bottom_cabinet_slgzfc_0 52x108 cm, desk_ohjotf_0 55x164 cm, shelf_rglkkf_0 49x172 cm, bottom_cabinet_jhymlr_0 40x118 cm, bottom_cabinet_nddvba_0 42x77 cm, desk_aduafr_0 64x152 cm, nightstand_roxnbe_0 53x78 cm, breakfast_table_rhjoby_0 117x290 cm, booth_xzrpar_0 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_1 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_2 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_3 69x131 cm, bottom_cabinet_olgoza_0 54x211 cm, pedestal_table_nlfgwe_0 107x107 cm, pedestal_table_nlfgwe_1 107x107 cm; partner and target side by side: each extent across the support <= depth - 6 cm and the two extents along it + 11 cm <= length, the sampler's cell / footprint margins) and (b) is wide enough to support every listed target set down centred on it (tiers: any_yaw = partner short side >= target long side, aligned = no overhang when the long axes align, centred = target overhangs but its contact patch is supported). Ranking: all test picks of the paired targets fit > fewer overhang / no-fit targets > fewer support misses > pinned (sampler-validated) > flags (tall / long / very thin) > support margin > size closest to the category median; pick 2 prefers a different geometry. Listed = min(viable, 12) models per category (viable = ready + fits every support + fits every test pick); further viable models, partial fits (some supports or some picks missed; not selected), rejected and not-ready models are named in the first row of the category. Evidence: runlogs/grasp_library_20260905/select/partners/partner_fit.json, partner_geometry.json (bboxes and fillable volumes read from the USDs), select_partners.py.

Two sub-types: small-under-small (the TOP object is grasped and set down on the bottom one: fries on platter, glass on coaster, teacup on saucer, bottle on tray) and small-under-big (object placed under furniture: sandal, briefcase, toy_figure, tennis_ball; partner = scene bed / desk / couch). Grasps: antipodal tabletop pipeline. Test spec pins toy_figure/cobfpg on desk_xhjsub_0 -> under bed_rrcvaq_0 (childs_room_0) (grasps.key toy_figure__cobfpg__t). Selection = grasp-library test instances (runlogs/grasp_library_20260905/select/test_instances.md): 2 picks per category, score = 2G+2V+T+R (max 25; G grasp, V visual, T task fit, R robustness); round 1 = original curated plan, 2 = category reused from another task, 3 = new category (single-model categories allowed). EVERY model with >= 1 AG-valid grasp is listed (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); models with no AG-valid grasp are not listed. Categories are ordered by their number of distinct geometries, descending. Duplicate check (select/duplicates.md): models judged the EXACT same asset count as one model in the counts and say 'exact duplicate of ...' in the duplicates column; texture/colour variants of one geometry are kept but marked 'same geometry as ...'.

Partner MODELS (2026-09-11): the rows below list, per partner category, the ready models (no unprocessed knowledge-base complaint) that (a) the instance sampler can place on the scene supports validated for IORS by the table-selection run so far plus the test table (15 supports: bottom_cabinet_slgzfc_0 52x108 cm, desk_ohjotf_0 55x164 cm, shelf_rglkkf_0 49x172 cm, bottom_cabinet_jhymlr_0 40x118 cm, bottom_cabinet_nddvba_0 42x77 cm, desk_aduafr_0 64x152 cm, nightstand_roxnbe_0 53x78 cm, breakfast_table_rhjoby_0 117x290 cm, booth_xzrpar_0 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_1 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_2 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_3 69x131 cm, bottom_cabinet_olgoza_0 54x211 cm, pedestal_table_nlfgwe_0 107x107 cm, pedestal_table_nlfgwe_1 107x107 cm; partner and target side by side: each extent across the support <= depth - 6 cm and the two extents along it + 11 cm <= length, the sampler's cell / footprint margins) and (b) (small-under-small) is wide enough to support the grasped target set down centred on it (tiers as for ontop). Listed = min(viable, 12) models per category (viable = ready + fits every support + fits every test pick); further viable models, partial fits (some supports or some picks missed; not selected), rejected and not-ready models are named in the first row of the category. Grasps: tabletop insert pipeline (pinch from above so the body can go down into the container; flowers held by the upper stem, flower_stem_top). Pair = partner container. Test spec pins lemon/ovbcff -> bowl/belcml (grasps.key lemon__ovbcff__i). Selection = grasp-library test instances (runlogs/grasp_library_20260905/select/test_instances.md): 2 picks per category, score = 2G+2V+T+R (max 25; G grasp, V visual, T task fit, R robustness); round 1 = original curated plan, 2 = category reused from another task, 3 = new category (single-model categories allowed). EVERY model with >= 1 AG-valid grasp is listed (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); models with no AG-valid grasp are not listed. Categories are ordered by their number of distinct geometries, descending. Duplicate check (select/duplicates.md): models judged the EXACT same asset count as one model in the counts and say 'exact duplicate of ...' in the duplicates column; texture/colour variants of one geometry are kept but marked 'same geometry as ...'.

Ranking: all test picks of the paired targets fit > fewer overhang / no-fit targets > fewer support misses > pinned (sampler-validated) > flags (tall / long / very thin) > support margin > size closest to the category median; pick 2 prefers a different geometry. Listed = min(viable, 12) models per category (viable = ready + fits every support + fits every test pick); further viable models, partial fits (some supports or some picks missed; not selected), rejected and not-ready models are named in the first row of the category. inter_object_relation_satisfaction-3 (nextto)target837 (57)58 model ids listed; 1 exact duplicates counted once -> 57 models (bracket); 26 models are texture/colour variants of another listed model -> 37 distinct geometriesBDDL objects: target (grasped or pushed so NextTo holds, released), partner, table, floor, agent. Grasps: antipodal tabletop pipeline. Pair = partner category (salt_shaker <-> pepper_shaker are mutual). Test spec pins spatula/hkvsep -> soup_ladle/cfzneb (grasps.key spatula__hkvsep__t). Selection = grasp-library test instances (runlogs/grasp_library_20260905/select/test_instances.md): 2 picks per category, score = 2G+2V+T+R (max 25; G grasp, V visual, T task fit, R robustness); round 1 = original curated plan, 2 = category reused from another task, 3 = new category (single-model categories allowed). EVERY model with >= 1 AG-valid grasp is listed (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate, sorted by score); models with no AG-valid grasp are not listed. Categories are ordered by their number of distinct geometries, descending. Duplicate check (select/duplicates.md): models judged the EXACT same asset count as one model in the counts and say 'exact duplicate of ...' in the duplicates column; texture/colour variants of one geometry are kept but marked 'same geometry as ...'.

Scene partners (countertop / desk / bed / couch) are fixed scene objects; object partners are listed per model below (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate as for the targets; PINNED = pinned in task_custom_lists.json). Partner MODELS (2026-09-11): the rows below list, per partner category, the ready models (no unprocessed knowledge-base complaint) that (a) the instance sampler can place on the scene supports validated for IORS by the table-selection run so far plus the test table (15 supports: bottom_cabinet_slgzfc_0 52x108 cm, desk_ohjotf_0 55x164 cm, shelf_rglkkf_0 49x172 cm, bottom_cabinet_jhymlr_0 40x118 cm, bottom_cabinet_nddvba_0 42x77 cm, desk_aduafr_0 64x152 cm, nightstand_roxnbe_0 53x78 cm, breakfast_table_rhjoby_0 117x290 cm, booth_xzrpar_0 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_1 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_2 69x131 cm, booth_xzrpar_3 69x131 cm, bottom_cabinet_olgoza_0 54x211 cm, pedestal_table_nlfgwe_0 107x107 cm, pedestal_table_nlfgwe_1 107x107 cm; partner and target side by side: each extent across the support <= depth - 6 cm and the two extents along it + 11 cm <= length, the sampler's cell / footprint margins) and (b) gives a NextTo bound mean(dims_a + dims_b)/6 above the sampler's 2 cm goal gap (gap_ok; gap_tight rows say which pairs need a smaller nextto_gap). Ranking: all test picks of the paired targets fit > fewer overhang / no-fit targets > fewer support misses > pinned (sampler-validated) > flags (tall / long / very thin) > support margin > size closest to the category median; pick 2 prefers a different geometry. Listed = min(viable, 12) models per category (viable = ready + fits every support + fits every test pick); further viable models, partial fits (some supports or some picks missed; not selected), rejected and not-ready models are named in the first row of the category. Evidence: runlogs/grasp_library_20260905/select/partners/partner_fit.json, partner_geometry.json (bboxes and fillable volumes read from the USDs), select_partners.py.

inter_object_relation_satisfaction-3 (nextto)floor00fixed scene object: house_single_floor: floor of dining_room_0; other scenes: floor of the room of the bound table (see the table row)
inter_object_relation_satisfaction-4 (touching)target821 (34)34 model ids listed; 0 exact duplicates counted once -> 34 models (bracket); 13 models are texture/colour variants of another listed model -> 21 distinct geometriesBDDL objects: target (pushed - or grasped and set down - until rigid contact (Touching) with the partner, released), partner (must not move > 5 mm at the goal settle), table, floor, agent; both poses measured only. The sampler puts the partner on the robot's left with a 10-25 cm gap and the goal translates the target sideways until the hulls touch (ispatialgym/sampling/tasks/iors.py). Test spec pins can_of_baking_mix/{blrqqz, orwvfx} -> board_game/{eoywpy, gcfkqa}. Selection (2026-09-11, runlogs/iors_touching_selection_20260911): same rules as nextto - target = ready tabletop object that is pinchable in its rest pose (smallest horizontal extent <= 8.9 cm, the antipodal pipeline's width limit) and stays upright when pushed at its near face (flat base >= 25% of the footprint, height <= 3 x its smallest horizontal extent, no rolling body), long side <= 30.0 cm, semantically paired with a partner category; 2 picks per category. Round 1 = 4 categories unused by any other task (incl. the parallel world-alignment candidate list), >= 2 distinct valid models; round 2 = 2 categories that another task uses in its round 1 (disembedding r1 targets not reused elsewhere), >= 2 valid models; round 3 = 2 categories with any overlap, single-model categories allowed. Pairs: r1: can_of_baking_mix -> board_game; r1: box_of_baking_powder -> kitchen_analog_scale; r1: box_of_coffee -> jar_of_grains; r1: box_of_vegetable_juice -> pop_case; r2: box_of_sanitary_napkins -> box_of_tissues; r2: carton_of_milk -> box_of_cookies; r3: teacup -> teapot; r3: bottle_of_medicine -> first_aid_kit. Rounds 2-3 reuse the tabletop grasp test of that category (result key, AG-valid / clean, selection score, reviewer note); round-1 categories have no grasp test (the touching oracle pushes) and were checked on textured renders (runlogs/iors_touching_selection_20260911/renders/grids). EVERY ready single-link model of a chosen category is listed (selection = pick 1 / pick 2 / alternate / candidate); models failing the touching check are named with the reason in the first row of the category. Categories are ordered by round, then by their number of distinct geometries. Duplicate check: reviewed categories use select/duplicates.md, fresh categories the vertex hash / texture md5 of the USD plus the renders (same geometry, texture/colour variant). Considered and not taken: paintbrush -> bucket_of_paint (brush 0.9-1.3 cm thick: not pushable / not AG-graspable); toilet_paper -> tissue_dispenser (2 of 4 rolls untextured grey, dispensers plain dark boxes); can_of_beans (its two models are the same asset); bottle_of_whiskey, bottle_of_soup, round_bottom_flask, erlenmeyer_flask (glass / breakable or round base / > 2.8 x aspect); eggplant, zucchini, gourd, sweet_corn, firewood, pencil_case, screwdriver (roll when pushed); carving_knife (blade a few mm thick: no push face), post_it, tag, table_knife, hard_drive (< 2.5 cm thick); test_tube_rack, shoe_box, storage_box, gift_box, desk_phone, loudspeaker, plant_pot, bucket_of_paint, hiking_boot (usable partners but no fresh pinchable target category pairs with them; kept as alternatives); kettle (alternative tea partner: 2 ready dark stovetop kettles, 18 x 16 x 17 cm). Method and per-model evidence: runlogs/iors_touching_selection_20260911/scripts/select_touching.py, touching_selection.json, candidate_pool.json, model_geometry.json, used_categories.json.
